payout.heading: Support this work
payout.note: These write-ups are researched and published with no paywall, sponsor, or tracking. If one saved you an afternoon, a small tip keeps them coming.
payout.note_on_config: The only monetization channel this stack can run unattended: a receive address in the article itself. No payment processor, no new secret, no owner action between a reader deciding to give and the money landing. Off by default -- turn it on once you have read the footer text, since it publishes under your byline. The address is checksum-validated (base58check for TRC-20, EIP-55 for ERC-20) before it can reach a reader; a malformed one omits the footer rather than publishing an address that would burn a reader's funds.

backfill.note_on_config: Adds the same payout footer to articles published before the footer existed. The back catalogue is where most readers already are -- 1,949 lifetime views across 11 posts, 85% of it on a single evergreen post -- and none of it carried an ask. Reuses DEV_TO_API_KEY via PUT /api/articles/{id}: no new secret, no owner action, no LLM call, and no new writing. Editing does not change published_at, so nothing is re-surfaced in the feed. A post whose body opens with YAML front matter is skipped, because Forem re-reads title and tags from that block on save and clears the tag list first. Gated on payout.enabled: if there is no footer shipping, there is nothing to backfill.

receipt_check.note_on_config: Verifies from outside that published posts actually carry the ask. Every other signal is the bot reporting on its own work: backfill computes 'remaining' from the same fetch it acts on, so when that fetch was wrong the work and the claim were wrong together and agreed. That hid a total failure for cycles #1760-#1773, with remaining: 0 while no post on the account had a footer. This re-reads each post through the unauthenticated GET /api/articles/{id} -- no key, no shared serializer with the writer. It never writes and never repairs: repair is backfill's job, and merging them would rebuild the same self-reporting blind spot one layer up. max_per_cycle is a SAMPLE size, not coverage: with 13 posts and a cap of 5 sorted by views, eight posts could never be read in any cycle while last_reason said 'all_verified'. Selection now rotates -- busiest post every cycle, remaining slots to the least-recently-verified -- so read covered/published_total and known_without_footer, not checked. known_without_footer persists across cycles: a gap found once must not vanish because the rotation moved past it. stale_after_hours expires an observation so coverage_complete cannot latch true on one old read; set 0 to disable expiry.

attribution.note_on_config: Records what was published when on-chain money arrived. Writes nothing unless wallet.last_received_usd > 0, so it cannot invent revenue. A TRC-20 transfer carries no memo, so every record is labelled confidence: correlated -- it is which posts were live when money landed, not proof of which one earned it. Read the count beside each total before believing an ordering: one receipt is one receipt.

requirements: Every lead must move a digital product toward earning without the owner in the loop.
Rank by how little owner action each unit of income needs, not by headline upside.
Name where the money lands, and prefer stablecoin to the address this project already publishes.
State every cost and every manual setup step out loud; zero budget is the constraint.
Never suggest selling the owner's hours: a rate per hour is a job, not passive income.
Stay inside policy: no social posting, no trading, no minting, no cold outreach.
Do not count discovery, pipeline, or speculative upside as earnings. On-chain or nothing.
product_shapes: browser extension solving one specific annoyance
static web tool that runs entirely client-side
template, preset, or asset pack for a tool people already use
developer library or plugin for an existing ecosystem
self-hostable script the buyer runs on their own machine
data set or reference compiled once and sold as a download
monetization_patterns: Ship the tool free and sell the upgrade: the free tier buys discovery the owner cannot.
One-time licence for a digital download, delivered by the storefront with no owner action.
Put the published receive address on the product page and in the README, so a user can pay with no platform at all.
Sell a template, preset, or asset pack built once and downloaded many times.
Charge for the paid tier of a tool whose free tier costs nothing per user to run.
List the same product on every zero-cost channel, since the artifact is already built.
underserved_focus: storefronts that settle stablecoin straight to the seller's own wallet, no custodian
one-task tools that solve a single annoyance well enough to be worth paying for
products with zero marginal cost per user, so the free tier can stay free forever
channels that are free to list on and have no approval queue to fail
paying users who never open a storefront and would rather send stablecoin directly
distribution with real organic discovery, so reach does not need ad spend
products whose buyers are developers, since that is the audience already reached
strategy_playbook: Build the product once, then spend every later cycle on distribution rather than on more product.
Keep marginal cost per user at zero: client-side code, free hosting, free scheduler. Every dollar in is margin.
Put the receive path on the artifact itself -- product page, README, article footer -- not only on a storefront.
List on the free channels first; pay a listing fee only where discovery is worth it, and say what it cost.
Let the articles this bot already publishes do the marketing: the problem is the post, the product is the fix.
Price once and leave it. A price that needs renegotiating per buyer is a service in disguise.
Measure only what arrives on-chain. Listings, views and pipeline are not revenue.
avoid_patterns: Selling the owner's hours: freelance postings, contract work, retainers, consulting. Income per unit of work is a job.
Anything requiring paid infrastructure, a monthly fee, or a credit-card-gated tier.
Custodial payment processors that hold the money before the owner does, and anything demanding KYC to receive.
Platforms that are dead, seized, or unverifiable. Sellix was seized in 2024 and is still widely recommended.
Trading, minting, yield farming, staking and airdrops: refused in code, and not a product business.
Offers needing a large audience, ad spend, or a following the owner does not have.
Anything promising passive income without a product that delivers something.

reference_sources.takeaway: The viable path is not easy money; it is rare skill, specialization, automation, retainers, async work, and results-based delivery.

reference_sources.title: OpenRouter free model list
reference_sources.takeaway: Free (:free) models are capped at 20 req/min and only 50 req/day unless the account has ever purchased $10 in credits (then 1,000/day) -- verify current limit before relying on volume.

reference_sources.title: Google AI Studio (Gemini API)
reference_sources.takeaway: No credit card required. Gemini 2.5 Flash free tier is roughly 1,500 requests/day; much higher daily ceiling than OpenRouter's free chain -- verify current limit.

reference_sources.title: Cerebras Cloud free tier
reference_sources.takeaway: No credit card required. Roughly 1M tokens/day and 14,400 requests/day per model -- verify current limit.

llm.note: All-free model chain, ordered per role in bot/llm.py _OPENROUTER_MODELS_BY_ROLE. openrouter/free -- the free auto-router -- leads every chain: it picks the best zero-cost model per request and filters for the features the request needs, so model choice tracks the live catalogue. openrouter/auto is deliberately NOT used: its candidate set includes paid models and it bills at the routed model's rate. Named free models (led by minimax/minimax-m3:free, 1M ctx, native response_format + tools) follow as fallback for when the router is rate-limited; on 402/429/404 the client steps down the rest of the role's free chain before changing provider.

evolution.note: LLM code proposals are committed to a review branch (branch_prefix/<version>-<utc>) and never to main. Merge the branch to apply. Writes are restricted to bot/, docs/, config/, requirements.txt, version.txt; bot/main.py, bot/llm.py, bot/status.py, bot/commands.py, bot/evolution.py, bot/git_utils.py and .github/ can never be written. Engine is the free OpenRouter 'upgrade' chain led by the openrouter/free auto-router; no paid model.
